title: operations with integers (addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, and order of operations)

lesson.title: Positives, Negatives, and How They Play Together

steps.say: Picture a January morning in Kelowna. At seven in the morning your phone says it's negative four degrees Celsius — cold enough to see your breath. By the afternoon it's plus nine degrees and you've taken your jacket off. How much warmer did it get? That question is exactly why we need integers: numbers that go below zero, not just above.

visual.caption: From negative four in the morning up to positive nine in the afternoon

steps.say: Look at the number line. To get from negative four up to positive nine, you walk four steps to reach zero, then nine more steps. Four plus nine is thirteen. So nine minus negative four equals thirteen degrees of warming. Here's the big idea: subtracting a negative is the same as adding. Taking away a debt makes you richer.

visual.caption: Both sides weigh the same — subtracting a negative is adding

steps.say: Now the other direction. Say you have twelve dollars on your transit card and you tap on for a five dollar trip. That trip is a negative five. Twelve plus negative five equals seven. So adding a negative is the same as subtracting — you slide left on the number line instead of right.

visual.caption: Twelve dollars, minus a five dollar trip, leaves seven

steps.say: Next, multiplying. Imagine you owe your brother three dollars, and you owe him that same three dollars four separate times. That's four groups of negative three, which is negative twelve. So when the signs are different — one positive, one negative — the answer comes out negative.

visual.caption: Four groups of a three dollar debt — that's negative twelve

steps.say: But what if both signs are negative? Negative three times negative four equals positive twelve. Think of it as taking away four debts of three dollars — if the debts vanish, you're twelve dollars better off. Same rule for dividing: negative twelve divided by negative four is positive three, and negative twelve divided by four is negative three. Just remember — same signs give a positive, different signs give a negative.

visual.caption: Two negatives flip you all the way over to the positive side

steps.say: Now let's put it all together with order of operations. The order is brackets first, then multiply and divide left to right, then add and subtract left to right. Try this one: twelve minus three times negative two. Multiplication goes first, so three times negative two is negative six. Now we have twelve minus negative six, and subtracting a negative is adding — so the answer is eighteen.

visual.caption: Multiply first, then subtract — and subtracting negative six adds six

steps.say: One more, a little tougher. Negative eight plus three, in brackets, times two, minus negative ten divided by five. Brackets first: negative eight plus three is negative five. Then the multiply and divide: negative five times two is negative ten, and negative ten divided by five is negative two. So now it reads negative ten minus negative two, which is negative ten plus two, and that lands on negative eight.

visual.caption: From negative ten, adding two brings us up to negative eight

steps.say: So here's the whole lesson in one breath: adding a negative walks you left, subtracting a negative walks you right, same signs multiply or divide to a positive, different signs to a negative — and always do the brackets first.

lesson.answer: Subtracting a negative adds; same signs make a positive, different signs make a negative — and brackets always go first.

practice.question: One January morning in Prince George the temperature is negative eleven degrees Celsius. During the day it warms up fourteen degrees, then in the evening it drops three degrees each hour for two hours. Work out: -11 + 14 - 3 × 2. What is the evening temperature?
practice.answer: -3 °C. Multiply first: 3 × 2 = 6. Then left to right: -11 + 14 = 3, and 3 - 6 = -3.
